clue.text: 26 is after Fat Controller

indicators.note: the brother follows the word for fat, so it comes second in the answer

parts.note: fat means big
the answer to 26 across is a monk, which is a brother

explanation.surface: Someone in clue 26 is chasing a portly railway boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at the Fat Controller of the Thomas the Tank Engine stories; 'Fat' and 'Controller' actually do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's all-seeing ruler in Nineteen Eighty-Four has become a byword for any controlling authority that watches everyone.

clue.text: One pushes half a tree trunk on lines supported by sleeper

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for sleeper sits beneath, holding up the rest
only the first half of the word for a tree trunk is used

parts.note: a butt is the base of a tree trunk
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
a dozer is someone who sleeps

explanation.surface: A logger shoves part of a trunk along railway lines laid on sleepers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeper' and 'lines' suggest railways, but the sleeper is a person dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulldozer is a tractor with a broad blade that pushes earth and debris.

clue.text: Happy to work on root of garden flower

parts.note: glad means happy
to do is to work

indicators.note: the root is the bottom, the final letter of garden

explanation.surface: A gardener is pleased to tend the roots of their flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word. In a down clue the root of 'garden' is its last letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladdon is a wild iris, the stinking iris, a flowering plant.

clue.text: Leg-side player in sign of danger is officially not out

parts.note: on is the cricket term for the leg side of the field

indicators.note: the player goes inside the sign of danger

parts.note: red is the colour that signals danger
a man is a player in a team or a piece in a game

explanation.surface: A cricketer fielding on the leg side is given not out amid warnings.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'not out' look like a batting verdict; it means held in custody, not released.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held pending trial has not been released, so they are officially not out of custody.

clue.text: One's up in it, to a degree

definitions.text: One's up in it, to a degree

parts.words: One's up in it, to a degree
parts.note: a student is said to be 'up' at university, studying towards a degree

explanation.definitionFit: University study leads to a degree, and British students are said to go 'up' to university.

clue.text: Cohesive reasoning holds up proof

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top
the two words hold the answer's letters within them

explanation.surface: Coherent argument backs up evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' picks ESIVER from 'cohESIVE Reasoning'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a revise is a further proof taken after corrections have been made.

clue.text: I envisage there'll be no time for guide

indicators.note: the word for guide is to lose a letter, since that letter will not be there

parts.note: to guide is to steer

explanation.surface: A traveller says they can picture a guide who has no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the seer speaking: a prophet is the one who says 'I envisage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet or visionary foresees the future, so the words 'I envisage' are what such a person would declare.

clue.text: Affected by the City's noon crash

indicators.note: a crash scatters the letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: The financial district is shaken by a market crash at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges THE, CITYS and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something synthetic is artificial or put on, which is what affected means of behaviour.

clue.text: Cover of The Listener?

parts.note: looks like a magazine cover, but the listener is the organ of hearing and the cover keeps it warm

explanation.definitionFit: These are pads worn over the ears to keep them warm, a covering for what listens.

clue.text: Golfer played round — a quiet game

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the next pieces, enclosing them
played suggests the letters of golfer being worked into a new order

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A golfer finishes a round and then plays a quiet game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' and 'round' both look like golf talk; the first rearranges the golfer's letters and the second wraps them around A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's playground pastime in which players vault over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: Literally, Evry, where such as 12 grows

parts.note: taken letter by letter, the French town name Evry is the letter V placed inside ERY, which is what the answer spells out

explanation.surface: A note about the French town of Evry being where a certain wine is grown.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read as instructions, the answer says 'V in ERY', and following them builds EVRY. 12 across is ZINFANDEL, a grape.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinery is a greenhouse or plot for growing vines, and the 12 across grape grows on vines.

clue.text: Notes one finished?

parts.note: do (doh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
a second do, since the plural asks for two notes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a set of notes marks the end of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The extinct bird is the classic thing that is 'finished'; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless bird of Mauritius died out completely, so it is the proverbial creature that is done for.

clue.text: Always problem about tea: it's miles ahead and I'm puffed!

indicators.note: the abbreviation for miles goes in front of everything else

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

indicators.note: the word for problem sits around the word for tea

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A runner, miles in front, gasps that they are out of breath while sipping tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm puffed' sounds like breathlessness but is the pipe speaking: a smoker puffs on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A meerschaum is a tobacco pipe carved from white clay, so it is something a smoker puffs at.

clue.text: Unknown field Ann played makes one blush

parts.note: Z is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

indicators.note: played signals the letters being shuffled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone called Ann plays in an unfamiliar field and ends up embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges FIELD and ANN into INFANDEL. 'makes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This grape gives a pink wine in its white style, and pale pink wine is known as blush.

clue.text: 1 ac associated with The Archers?

parts.note: 1 across can be read as a fat brother, and this portly friar belonged to Robin Hood's band of archers

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Archers' is a long-running BBC radio soap; here it means Robin Hood's outlaws.
explanation.definitionFit: The stout friar of the Robin Hood legend is a fat brother among the outlaw archers.

clue.text: Post office workers

definitions.meaning: the people employed in an office

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a wooden pole and the body of employees in an organisation.

clue.text: Crawler's trap at bottom of Channel

indicators.note: in a down clue the trap sits below the channel

parts.note: a funnel channels liquid
a web is a spider's trap

explanation.surface: A spider spins its trap at the bottom of the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link (is). 'Channel' looks like the sea, but means a funnel.
explanation.definitionFit: A funnel-web is a venomous Australian spider, a creature that crawls.

clue.text: Short notices about, such a price for keyboard

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the price
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: spies means notices or spots
a nett price is one with nothing more to deduct

explanation.surface: Brief announcements around the price of a keyboard instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIES cut short gives SPIE, which goes about NETT to make SPI(NETT)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, a keyboard instrument, and this is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Excellent American team going round base

parts.note: rad is American slang for excellent

indicators.note: the team's Roman numeral is turned about

parts.note: XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A terrific US side travelling around a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' suggests a military camp but is the mathematical base of a number system; 'going round' turns the team's numeral about.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the radix is the base of a number system, ten for decimal.

clue.text: Orated, confused about Conservative style

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit round the abbreviation
confused suggests the letters of orated being jumbled

explanation.surface: A speaker talks muddledly about Tory style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes ARTDEO from ORATED, and C goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is a decorative design style of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: One's clean above it

parts.note: a person with a clean record is said to be beyond doubt or mistrust, 'above' it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'above suspicion' describes someone so clean nobody could distrust them.

clue.text: Jeopardise position at head of averages, failing in August

indicators.note: the letter fails to appear in the word for august

parts.note: august means stately or majestic, which imperial also means

indicators.note: the letter in position at the head of averages is its first

explanation.surface: A cricketer risks top place in the batting averages after a poor August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month, but is the adjective meaning majestic.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to put in danger, which is what jeopardise means.

clue.text: Grand king eating in French or Polish town

indicators.note: the two letters take in the French word, enclosing it

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand (a thousand)
K is the chess abbreviation for king
dans is French for in

explanation.surface: A great king dines in either France or Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link; 'French' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a port city on the Baltic coast of Poland.

clue.text: What's ultimately filled in downpours

parts.note: a channel in the street that heavy rain eventually fills

explanation.definitionFit: A street gutter channel built to carry away rainwater is what fills during heavy rain.

clue.text: Mock taken around start of summer recess

indicators.note: the word for mock is wrapped around the next letter

parts.note: to ape is to mock by imitating

indicators.note: start of means take the first letter of summer

explanation.surface: Someone is teased at the beginning of the summer holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' looks like a school break, chiming with 'summer', but is a church recess.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted semicircular recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Reportedly want success; possibly a gold disc

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to want success is to seek a win

explanation.surface: Musicians said to be chasing success might win a gold record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold disc' suggests a music award, but it is a small shiny spangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequin is a small shiny disc sewn onto clothing, often gold-coloured.

clue.text: With nightwear off, without clothing at last?

definitions.text: With nightwear off, without clothing at last?

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of nightwear being disordered
the anagram is made without one letter, which is removed
at last means take the final letter of clothing

explanation.surface: Once the pyjamas come off, someone is finally wearing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGHTWEAR without G (the last letter of 'clothing') rearranges to give the answer, and the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means naked, which is what remains once the nightwear is off.

clue.text: Originally, man of note kept one in order

indicators.note: originally means take the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: A distinguished man was kept in order from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is a religious order, not tidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk is a member of a religious order of brothers.

clue.text: Wherein only the very best, best friends officially gather

definitions.text: Wherein only the very best, best friends officially gather

parts.words: Wherein only the very best, best friends officially gather
parts.note: dogs are man's best friend, and the elite pedigrees are registered with this British body

explanation.definitionFit: This UK body registers pedigree dogs and runs Crufts, so the finest dogs are officially gathered there.
